notes: Round 3, after library round 25 (L126). (1) assumption:dot is still the right fact. DotF16 is listed, as restated, in num.md's 'Facts the library states' and in the reviewer's table for float16 operands into float32 with maxImpreciseAcc = 0 and any precision. It is now 'forall p, DotLiftAcc P <f16, f16, f32, p, 0> relDot16 absDot16', with relDot16 and absDot16 unchanged. The field's docstring and the README state it as DotLiftAcc, with L = |acc| + sum liftMag a * liftMag b. (2) spec: the tolerance is the same function tol K A, and A is now dotMag = sum mag16(va k) * mag16(vb k). mag16 is the library's liftMag .f16 by definition (rfl, checked in work/Lift.lean), so the specification counts magnitudes as the cited fact does. With no subnormal operand, mag16 q = |q| (work/Lift.lean, mag16_of_normal), so every figure of round 2 stands: 1.26e-4 at K = 512, 1.01e-3 at 4096, below 0.21% up to 2^13, and the rejection of a bfloat16-rounded result on normal one-sign inputs. The README's bound on a lifted term, |x*y| + 2^-14*(|x| + |y|) + 2^-28, is proved in work/Lift.lean (mag16_mul_le). Post still rejects a kernel that flushes subnormal float16 operands to zero: one product 2^-15 * 1 errs by 2^-15 against tol(2^13, 2^-14) < 2^-15 (work/Lift.lean). On the host's randn inputs a subnormal float16 is rare (about 5e-5 of values), and it adds at most about 2^-14*|partner| to A, so the tolerance's meaning at the host's sizes is unchanged. (3) assumption:dot_total re-opened only through the files docs/rules/num.md and lean/TVA/Rules/Num.lean; DotTotal and its listing are unchanged. (4) The kernel's Lean changes are the new defs mag16 and dotMag (dotAbs removed), the lemmas in Basic.lean (partA over liftV, acc_step on the restated fact) and a docstring in Program.lean. There is no instance, notation, attribute or export. The model, launch, conditions and map are unchanged (the gate snapshots show their items' digests as before). main, consistent and satisfiable depend only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. (5) F7 (r-matmul2's LIBRARY_REPORT on DotF16) is REFERRED to L126, which round 25 fixed by restating DotF16 relative to lifted magnitudes, and the claim is re-proved on it, so the report is settled.
